proposed_widenings.name: AnchorTarget { kind: "self" }
proposed_widenings.justification: Contingency's anchor is the caster themselves, not a location or area. AnchorTarget currently only has 'location' and 'area' variants.
proposed_widenings.evidence: The contingent spell takes effect only on you

proposed_widenings.name: AnchoredEvent { kind: "player_described_condition"; description: string }
proposed_widenings.justification: Contingency's trigger is an arbitrary free-form condition described by the player at cast time. The current AnchoredEvent closed enum (physical_contact, enters_area) cannot represent open-ended trigger conditions. This is a genuine structural gap: the condition predicate is not a deterministic engine-evaluable formula but a natural-language description adjudicated at runtime.
proposed_widenings.evidence: The contingent spell takes effect when a certain trigger occurs. You describe that trigger when you cast the two spells. For example, a Contingency cast with Water Breathing might stipulate that Water Breathing comes into effect when you are engulfed in water or a similar liquid.

proposed_widenings.name: AnchoredSignal { kind: "stored_spell_release" }
proposed_widenings.justification: The signal emitted when the trigger fires is 'release the stored contingent spell on the caster'. AnchoredSignal only has 'audible' and 'mental'. The stored spell is the payload, not a notification signal.
proposed_widenings.evidence: The contingent spell takes effect immediately after the trigger occurs for the first time, whether or not you want it to, and then Contingency ends.

proposed_widenings.name: stored_spell_reference — cast-time constrained spell capture
proposed_widenings.justification: Contingency captures a second spell at cast time (constrained to: level ≤5, action casting time, self-targetable). This spell's full payload is held and released on trigger. No existing surface type represents a 'choose a spell at cast time, apply constraint filter, hold payload for deferred release' pattern.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Choose a spell of level 5 or lower that you can cast, that has a casting time of an action, and that can target you. You cast that spell—called the contingent spell—as part of casting Contingency

proposed_widenings.name: dual_slot_cast — simultaneous dual spell-slot consumption
proposed_widenings.justification: Casting Contingency expends two spell slots simultaneously: one L6 slot for Contingency and one L1–5 slot for the contingent spell. The current surface models a single spell_slot resource per cast. No multi-slot consumption pattern exists.

notes: anchored_trigger is structurally the closest family (store-at-cast → release-on-event). However, Contingency cannot be honestly encoded in it for two fundamental reasons: (1) The trigger predicate is genuinely open-ended — any condition the player can articulate — not a closed spatial or physical event. Representing this as a closed-enum variant would require a free-text fallback, which breaks the closed-atom principle. (2) The payload held is a full spell, not a notification signal. The signal union (audible/mental) is inappropriate for spell release. The self-anchor, dual-slot cost, and stored-spell constraint filter are additional surface widenings that compound the structural gaps. This unit is best revisited once the taxonomy explicitly models a 'stored_spell' attachment, a constraint-filtered spell reference, and a mechanism for open or semi-open trigger predicates.
